Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Goal: Validate model fit for Avery Labs’ product QA workload (short customer support Q&A and product attribute extraction).
2) Recommended initial models: Llama-3-Chat-13B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct-7B, and a smaller supervised fine-tune baseline (for latency tests). See links below for benchmark profiles.
3) Redwood evals: we can run a customer-specific eval on your dataset (format: CSV with id, input, expected_output). We’ll provide a prompt set and scoring rubric; expected OSS-friendly tooling is the Redwood eval runner.
4) Data we need from you: 200-500 representative examples for phase 1, an internal priority metric (exact match vs. semantic F1), and any safety/PII handling notes.
5) Timeline: if we get the dataset by Tue 3/17, we can run the initial evals and share results by Friday 3/20.

Attachments: I’ve included a prompt set starter and a sample eval dataset template.

Next immediate step: can you confirm dataset availability and preferred scoring metric? If you want, Vivek can spin up a trial Redwood eval run and share the command and results.

Thanks — talk soon.

Samantha —

Great — thanks for the fast turnaround. Answers inline below and attached the benchmark links you asked for.

- Weighting suggestion: for phase 1 we recommend 70% structured exact-match, 30% semantic F1 for free-text. That keeps the initial pass focused on the attributes you care about while still surfacing quality differences in generative responses. We can tune after the first run.
- PII: please mask full emails and any full credit-card or SSN-like strings. First names and non-sensitive IDs are fine. Redwood will not persist raw dataset beyond the eval run unless you request longer retention. We can also run inside your Private deployment or Dedicated pool if you need more isolation.
- Benchmark links: 
  * Llama-3-Chat-13B performance profile: https://models.redwood.ai/llama3-13b/profile
  * Mistral-Instruct-7B profile: https://models.redwood.ai/mistral-7b/profile
  * Redwood eval best practices doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/best-practices

I’ve attached a starter prompt_set_product_qa_v1.txt with 10 prompt templates and scoring hints. We’ll use that as the first pass. Vivek — can you add the exact Redwood eval-runner commands (container/CLI) and the JSON scoring config we typically use for a mixed exact/semantic rubric?

If everything looks good, Samantha — please send the masked CSV to this thread and we’ll schedule the run for Wed morning.

—
Marissa

Hi Samantha —

I’m Vivek (Solutions Engineer) — looping in the technical details so you have a reproducible run. Below is the minimal path to run the customer-specific eval on Redwood and the scoring config we recommend.

1) Dataset format: CSV with columns: id, input, expected_output. UTF-8, newline-delimited, no embedded newlines in cells. Example attached in the template.

2) Prompt set: use prompt_set_product_qa_v1.txt — each row is a template. The runner will expand templates against the input column.

3) Scoring config (we’ll share as JSON in the Drive link but here’s the rubric):
   - "structured_fields": exact_match, weight 0.7 (fields: sku, attribute_value, status)
   - "free_text": semantic_similarity (embedding-based cosine + human spot checks), weight 0.3
   - Thresholds: pass if weighted_score >= 0.75; flag if free_text similarity < 0.6 for manual review.

4) Redwood eval-runner CLI (example):
   docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data redwood/eval-runner:stable \n     --dataset /data/avery_eval_dataset_v1.csv \n     --prompts /data/prompt_set_product_qa_v1.txt \n     --model llama3-chat-13b-q8_0 \n     --scoring-config /data/avery_scoring_config.json \n     --output /data/avery_eval_results.jsonl

5) Models to run: we suggest running the three configs Marissa listed. For latency/throughput, run the smaller supervised baseline and Mistral-7B in Dedicated mode if you want consistent perf numbers.

6) Data handling: Redwood will mount the dataset only for the run and delete after results delivery. If you need retention, request explicit agreement. For PII, please mask emails and sensitive identifiers; we can also run in your Private deployment.

Next steps: if you post the masked CSV to the Drive folder (or drop it in this thread), I’ll schedule the run Wednesday 9am PT and share the command output and a short report (confusion table + example pass/fail cases).

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
